evidence: PROBE REPRODUCTION. The predecessor's mask is a hand-checkable ellipse on the exposed (lower) cut face of 05-cut+500ms; running it on r3 returns n=1881, mean (223.8, 117.6, 95.7), R>=255 50.0%, lumMedian 142.7, dark5 54.1, ratio 2.64 -- against the predecessor's n=1867, (230.7, 118.9, 96.9), 49.7%, 143.0, 63.2, 2.26. Same probe on plate-01's flesh box (560-800, 380-520) returns mean (192.3, 70.7, 55.4), R>=255 0.7%, lumMedian 85.4 against their (188.4, 72.2, 55.8), 0.6%, 85.8. The method is theirs. (1) CLIPPING, WATERMELON -- DID NOT MOVE. r3 49.7% (mine 50.0%) -> r4 49.3% (same 0.55-of-face rule) / 42.0% (same absolute window). Target <5%, plate-01 inner-0.55 0.3%. On a tight core-0.80 mask of the same face: 18.3% -> 20.5% (plate-01 0.3%). The exposure contract cut the key 7.7 -> 3.40 and this number moved 0.4 points. (2) COLOUR WENT SLIGHTLY BACKWARDS. Same ellipse: G/R 0.549 -> 0.559, B/R 0.443 -> 0.454; plate-01 inner-0.55 is 0.274 / 0.146, plate-01 flesh box 0.368 / 0.288. The pulp is still a milky salmon. Decisive detail: the 1193 R=255 pixels on that face average (255, 165, 135) -- a pale pink-WHITE. The clipping is an achromatic wash (foam lift + wet spec + SSS) riding on top of the red, not a saturated red. (3) THE SAME FRAME PROVES THE MATERIAL IS RIGHT AND THE IRRADIANCE IS WRONG. The shadow-side (upper) cut face of the SAME melon in the SAME frame measures mean (104, 34, 14), G/R 0.323, R>=255 1.9%, lumMedian 39.0 -- that is plate-grade. Only the key-facing half blows. The contract block at stage.js:105 lists 'E, face-on to the CAMERA (cut faces) 0.704' and 'E, facing the KEY 1.565', and species.js:920 pins ripe at 'exactly the contract's face-on budget of 0.90'; 0.90 x 1.565 = 1.41 scene-linear against a 0.65 clip threshold, i.e. 2.2x over. The materials author's own predicted table at species.js:915 says R>=255 4.1%, mean (189.1, 70.5, 55.7), G/R 0.373. Measured: 49.3%, (218.0, 121.8, 99.0), 0.559. The model missed its headline number by 12x. (4) SEEDS -- IMPROVED, STILL SHORT. Darkest 5% of the same ellipse: 63.2 -> 45.3 (target <=25, plate-01 10.4). pctBelow lum 25: 0.0% -> 1.0% (plate-01 10.1%). Contrast med/p2 2.61 -> 3.35 on the ellipse, 4.79 vs plate-01's 6.04 on the core-0.80 mask. At 5x the seeds now read as black occluders, but the face under them is still lifted (core lumMedian 84.4 -> 112.1 against plate-01's 74.2). (5) CITRUS -- THE ONE PLACE THE COORDINATION ACTUALLY WORKED. Near half incl. peel, largest lum>45 component in box (170-300, 225-340) of 08-citrus-caps: r3 n=7288 mean (215.6, 139.7, 65.4) R>=255 48.3% -> r4 n=6150 mean (191.1, 116.1, 38.6) R>=255 19.1%. At lum>80: 57.2% -> 24.3%. That is a 29-point drop and it more than undoes the 15-point regression the r3 verdict named (their scale: 39.3 -> 54.0 -> ~21). At 5x the peel now has a real terminator, a dark left flank and readable pore texture where r3 was a featureless cream blob. Still ~4x the <5% target; plate-02's lemon body measures R>=255 0.0%. (6) PITH RING -- IN FAMILY NOW. 48-spoke peak-luminance probe over the 0.90R-1.25R band of the lower face: fraction of band pixels clipped white (all channels >=250) is 0.0% in BOTH r3 and r4, so the '67% clipped' figure was already dead before this round. Directional variation max/min 7.50 -> 6.26 against plate-01's watermelon pith 7.41 (plate-02 lemon peel 1.80); first-harmonic 29% -> 48% against plate-01's 40%. Band mean luminance 37.8 -> 82.5 (plate-01 97.2) and band/core ratio 0.36 -> 0.69 (plate-01 1.22): the pith is no longer a dead stroke. (7) GLOBAL EXPOSURE CAME DOWN AS PROMISED. Whole melon body in 01: mean luminance 89.3 -> 74.8, R>=255 5.35% -> 5.11%. So the key cut landed everywhere the key drives -- skins, peel, body -- and landed nowhere on the cut face, which is the one surface the round was about. DID THE COORDINATION WORK? Half. The contract fixed the two authors' disagreement about the SKIN chain and is a genuine process win; it encoded a false premise about the CUT-FACE chain (that a cut face is camera-facing) and nothing in the pipeline enforces the premise, so the same cancellation happened again on the surface that matters most. BLIND: handed 05-cut+500ms and plate-01 unlabelled I pick the render in well under a second -- the lit half is a glowing pink disc with a soft white halo sitting on its upper edge and a cream outline around it; no watermelon does that. Second tell, new this round: the orange's pore texture in 08-citrus-caps is a regular grid of hard-edged square dots.
fix: In /home/claude/juice/src/fruit/species.js, re-solve the two flesh ramps at :920 against the KEY-facing irradiance, not the camera-facing one. The contract's own table gives E_R = 1.565 for a key-facing surface, so `ripe = vec3(0.9000, 0.1507, 0.1228)` must come down by 1.565/0.704 = 2.22x to about vec3(0.405, 0.0678, 0.0553), with `deep` to vec3(0.1305, 0.0230, 0.0192) to keep the 3.1x spread, and the lost mid-tone recovered through the `t` offset (0.618) rather than the top of the ramp. Then kill the achromatic wash that the R=255 pixels' mean (255,165,135) exposes: the foam whitening lift at weight 0.22 x vec3(0.085) and the wet run-off line at :~990 (`alb.mul(1.18).add(vec3(0.058,...))`) must both be gated by the same `capKey()` N.L term the pith already uses, so they cannot fire at full strength on the key-facing spoke. Re-run the exact ellipse probe above and require R>=255 under 5% AND G/R at 0.33 +/- 0.05 on the LIT half, measured with the shadow half (currently (104,34,14), G/R 0.323, R>=255 1.9%) as the in-frame control. Finally, the EXPOSURE CONTRACT block at stage.js:105 must state E for cut faces as a RANGE 0.136..1.565 with the clip budget solved at the top of it; as written it invites exactly this failure again.
notes: Score 46 -> 51. The citrus regression is fully repaired and then some, the pith ring now sits inside plate-01's own modulation family, and the shadow-side flesh is genuinely plate-grade -- those are four real, measured wins and they are why the score moves at all. But the single gap named in round 2 and again in round 3, red-channel clipping on the watermelon cut face, moved 49.7% -> 49.3%, and flesh milkiness moved the wrong way again. The EXPOSURE CONTRACT is a good instrument aimed at the wrong surface: it froze the number the two authors were fighting over and then applied a camera-facing irradiance to a face that is turned into the key.
